summary: The comma command selects an uncursed floor scroll of scare monster, but a JavaScript pickup preflight refuses the type before pickup.c:pickup_object can run its source branch. C counts a liftable subset first, marks an uncursed unused scroll as picked up once, then continues through lift_object and pick_obj. The full pickup_object source function also handles blessed and dusting scrolls, split stacks, corpses, artifacts, and ordinary objects.

source.branch: After pickup_object observes a visible floor object and passes chain, engulfer, artifact, and corpse checks, SCR_SCARE_MONSTER first calls carry_count with a consumed count and weight outputs. It returns -1 for an unliftable stack, splits a liftable subset before state change, unblesses a blessed scroll, changes spe from 0 to 1 for an uncursed unused scroll, or turns other scrolls to dust through trycall/useupf and returns 1. The selected case is the uncursed spe=0 path, followed by the ordinary lift_object/pick_obj/inventory message tail.
callers: pickup.c:pickup explicit floor-selection loop calls pickup_object and consumes its return to decide whether to continue; js/pickup.js:pickup calls js/pickup.js:pickup_object after preflightPickupObjects.
apply.c:use_whip and other pickup.c paths also call pickup_object, so special scroll behavior belongs in the source helper rather than a comma-command exception.
dependencies: pickup.c:carry_count returns the liftable count and writes old_wt/new_wt; js/pickup.js has carry_count, but the preflight currently blocks SCR_SCARE_MONSTER before it can be used.
obj.c:splitobj, obj.c:unbless, do.c:trycall, and invent.c:useupf provide consumed object/count or side-effect dependencies. Verify their current JavaScript signatures and caller order.
pickup.c:lift_object and pick_obj return decisions/objects consumed by pickup_object, and the ordinary pickup tail must remain aligned for every previously matching object class.

Remove the type refusal in preflightPickupObjects once the complete branch is in pickup_object; preserve sight-gated observe_object, artifact/corpse branches, telekinesis wording, object knowledge, and RNG order.

evidence: The saved v13 evaluation at 35deeae3b45298577e919836bfad5c2da681ab6b reports 46/47 screens and cursors, 2548/2556 RNG calls, and first stop at zero-based segment 0 step 46: “unsupported pickup: pickup() of a scroll of scare monster.” The immutable recording is challenges/cases/v13/uncursed-scare-scroll-pickup-reveals-use.session.json, SHA256 8d33dbd7f0e6a96a67141a7f29a30a2bd997dfe3218cda779f7e34adde9db32e.

The independent recipe wishes an explicitly uncursed scroll, drops its observed inventory letter p, then presses comma. The C recording step 46 shows the floor selector for a scroll labeled MAPIRO MAHAMA DIROMAT. Its setup comment and source trace identify the intended spe=1 arm; the screen alone does not expose spe, so implementation must verify state through source and focused replay.

Upstream nethack-c/upstream/src/pickup.c:1803-1888 defines pickup_object. The SCR_SCARE_MONSTER branch at 1832-1857 consumes carry_count, splits a liftable subset, handles blessed and uncursed-first-pickup states, or dusts the scroll. The shared tail at 1868-1888 lifts, extracts, prints, and returns. pickup.c explicit pickup callers at 784, 815, and 886 consume the return.

JavaScript js/pickup.js:preflightPickupObjects around lines 898-906 rejects SCR_SCARE_MONSTER before js/pickup.js:pickup_object, whose current source port skips the scroll arm and reaches lift_object directly. Existing helpers include carry_count, splitobj, unbless, trycall, and useupf; integrate them in C order and preserve all existing pickup behavior.
